metaDescription: Hotel Christmas decorating contractors for lobbies, atriums and porte-cochères in Ontario. Brand colours, overnight installs around check-in, full service.
h1: Hotel Christmas decorating contractors for lobbies, atriums and porte-cochères
intro: Hotel Christmas decorating contractors have one job: make the arrival look finished without ever getting in the way of a guest. We decorate hotel lobbies, atriums, porte-cochères, ballroom foyers and restaurant entrances across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara, from a single decorated lobby tree to a full exterior and interior program with a lit approach road. Everything is designed around the guest arrival.

Installs happen overnight, timed with your front office so the lift is out of the porte-cochère before the morning departures and the lobby tree is complete before the first check-in. Colour schemes follow your brand standard or the lobby finishes, so a corporate flag gets its approved look and an independent property gets something of its own. Reference photos come from our own installs, not a catalogue.

Everything is our own commercial-grade inventory, which lets us include maintenance all season at no charge. If a section of the canopy outline goes dark on a Saturday in December, we fix it. Takedown in the first three weeks of January, labelled storage in our warehouse and a multi-year agreement that locks price and dates are all standard. You get one number for the whole season.

challenges.title: Installs cannot disrupt guests
challenges.body: A hotel never closes, so a crew in the lobby at 2 p.m. is a problem. We work overnight, usually between late check-in and early departures, coordinate with the night manager and bell desk, protect floors and keep the porte-cochère open for taxis and airport shuttles while the lift is positioned off to one side.

challenges.title: Brand standards and GM approval
challenges.body: Flag properties have approved colour palettes and a GM who answers to an owner. We propose a scheme with photos from our own installs, match ribbon and lighting to the brand standard, and provide a written scope that can be forwarded for approval. Changes are easy before anything ships from our warehouse.

challenges.title: The display must be on every night
challenges.body: December is peak for weddings, corporate dinners and family stays, and a dark canopy or a half-lit lobby tree gets noticed. Maintenance is included on every program, with storm checks on the exterior and spares on the truck, so a fault is fixed quickly, usually the same day.

challenges.title: Storage and labour
challenges.body: Hotels have no spare room for a 16 ft tree and forty boxes of ornaments, and engineering staff have better things to do in November than fluff branches. We lease the decor, install it, remove it in January and store it in our warehouse, so housekeeping and engineering never touch it.

spaces.title: Lobby and atrium
spaces.body: A decorated pre-lit tree sized to the ceiling, often flanked by accent trees, with garland on the front desk and lit planters at the doors. Atrium trees of 16 to 20+ ft go up from a lift overnight. Colours match the brand or the stone, wood and metal of the lobby.

spaces.title: Porte-cochère and canopy
spaces.body: The canopy edge outlined in warm-white C9 or mini lights, columns wrapped in lit garland and wreaths centred between them. Coach and shuttle clearance is checked before anything is hung, and the circuit runs on a photocell so the arrival is lit from dusk without a staff member touching a switch.

spaces.title: Ballroom foyer and event spaces
spaces.body: Trees, garland and lit planters outside ballrooms and meeting rooms, placed to frame the doors for wedding and corporate photos without narrowing the pre-function space. Decor is secured against being moved by banquet setup and can be adjusted for a specific event on request.

spaces.title: Restaurant and bar
spaces.body: Smaller trees, garland on the host stand and railings, wreaths on glass and bistro lighting on patios and terraces. Dining-room decor is kept clear of service paths and heat sources, and the patio lighting is on the same timer as the exterior program.

spaces.title: Exterior approach and grounds
spaces.body: Tree wrapping along the driveway, lit cone trees at the entrance, roofline outlines on the main facade and lighting around fountains and signage so the property reads from the road. Mature trees are wrapped from a bucket truck so the canopy is lit, not just the trunk.

programs.name: Essentials
programs.body: A finished arrival for a limited-service or select-service hotel: a decorated lobby tree, wreaths at the entrance and lit garland on the canopy columns. Installed in one night, serviced all season and stored in January.
includes: Decorated pre-lit lobby tree, 9 to 12 ft
Lit wreaths at the main entrance
Garland on porte-cochère or canopy columns

programs.name: Signature
programs.body: A full-service property program: a taller lobby or atrium tree with accent trees, front-desk garland, lit planters, the porte-cochère outlined and the main facade or entrance trees lit so the hotel reads from the street.
includes: Lobby or atrium tree, 12 to 16 ft, with accent trees
Front desk and railing garland, lit planters
Entrance tree wrapping or cone trees

programs.name: Landmark
programs.body: For resort, conference and flagship properties: a 20+ ft atrium tree, themed lobby displays, guest photo moments, driveway tree wrapping, roofline outlines and restaurant, bar and patio decor, all coordinated to one brand-standard scheme.
includes: Atrium tree 16 to 20+ ft with custom scheme
Themed lobby display or photo moment
Full porte-cochère, facade and roofline lighting

Scope approved and dates reserved. Multi-year agreements lock price and schedule. Inventory is pulled, tested and labelled for your property in our warehouse.
Overnight installation coordinated with the front office and bell desk, exterior first, then lobby and event spaces, lit before the end of November.
Display runs on timers and photocells. Any fault fixed at no charge, storm checks on the exterior, and adjustments for specific events on request.
Takedown in the first three weeks on a date you choose, usually the first week for the lobby. Everything is labelled and stored for next season.

faqs.question: How do hotel lobby Christmas decorators install without disrupting guests?
faqs.answer: We work overnight, coordinated with your night manager. The crew arrives after the late check-in rush, protects the lobby floor, builds and decorates the tree, and is gone before early departures. Exterior work on the porte-cochère is scheduled so taxis and shuttles keep moving, with the lift positioned to one side and cones out. Most lobby programs are complete in one night; atrium trees and full exteriors may take two.

faqs.question: Can the decor match our brand standard colours?
faqs.answer: Yes. We match ribbon, ornaments and lighting to the approved palette and confirm colours on physical samples before anything ships, because a brand blue on screen and a lit tree at night are not the same thing. The written scope and reference photos can be forwarded to the brand or owner for sign-off. Independent properties get a scheme built around the lobby's finishes instead.

faqs.question: What does porte-cochere holiday lighting setup involve?
faqs.answer: We outline the canopy edge with commercial C9 or mini LED, wrap the columns in lit garland and hang wreaths between them, running the feed to a protected outlet on a photocell or timer. Before install we check coach and shuttle clearance, where the lift can sit without blocking the drive and how the lighting looks from the approach road. It is installed overnight and serviced at no charge all season.

faqs.question: Is atrium holiday decor leasing better than buying for a hotel?
faqs.answer: For most hotels, yes. Leasing puts design, the tree and decor, overnight installation, season maintenance, January removal and warehouse storage into one seasonal operating cost with no capital purchase and no storage room lost. Buying makes sense only if you have dry storage and want to run the same look for many years, and you still pay annually for setup, service and takedown. We show both options in the quote.

faqs.question: What happens if lights fail during a December wedding weekend?
faqs.answer: Call or text us and we fix it at no charge, usually the same day in December. Because the product is our own inventory, crews carry spare strings, plugs and tree sections and most faults are a swap on the first visit. Exterior checks also happen after major wind or ice storms without a call. A dark hotel entrance is treated as a priority over everything else on the list that day.

faqs.question: What does a hotel holiday decor program typically cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site visit. As a typical range, a 9 ft decorated lobby tree program starts around $1,500 per season, a full lobby and porte-cochère program runs into five figures, and resort or conference properties with atrium trees, themed displays and driveway lighting go higher. Tree height, linear footage, lift work and a one-season versus multi-year term are the drivers. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

ctaTitle: Book a site visit before the season fills
ctaBody: Hotel installs are scheduled from October and the best overnight slots go first. Call 519-266-6796 or send photos of the lobby and porte-cochère and we will reply within one business day with a design and a per-season price.

metaDescription: Condo lobby Christmas decorator for boards and managers across Ontario. Lobby trees, entrance canopies and courtyards, installed around the concierge.
h1: Condo lobby Christmas decorator for boards and property managers
intro: A condo lobby Christmas decorator has to satisfy a board, a property manager and several hundred residents who walk past the tree twice a day. We decorate condo and apartment lobbies, entrance canopies and courtyards across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara with a written scope the board can approve, a price that fits the budget cycle and a crew that installs around the concierge, not through them.

Multi-residential holiday decor setup is mostly about consistency and safety. A tree that matches the lobby finishes, is secured against tipping, keeps the vestibule clear for strollers and movers, and runs on a timer so it is never left on all night. For managers with several buildings, the same scheme across the portfolio means one approval and one invoice. Boards see photos from our own installs before approving.

Installs happen overnight or in the quiet middle of a weekday, scheduled with the concierge or superintendent so the loading dock and elevator are booked. Maintenance is included at no charge, takedown runs in the first three weeks of January and the decor is stored in our warehouse so no storage locker or mechanical room is given up. Residents simply arrive home to a finished lobby.

challenges.title: Board approval and budget timing
challenges.body: Boards approve a specific proposal, not an idea, and the budget was set last spring. We provide a written scope with tree size, scheme and reference photos from our own installs, priced per season or on a multi-year term, so the manager can table it at one meeting and get a decision.

challenges.title: Resident safety in a busy lobby
challenges.body: Strollers, dogs, movers and grocery carts all pass the tree. We secure trees against tipping, route cords under covers, keep the vestibule and accessible routes clear, use shatterproof ornaments and keep garland away from door closers and fire equipment. Timers switch the display off overnight.

challenges.title: Scheduling with the concierge and super
challenges.body: Elevators and loading docks are booked, and a crew that shows up unannounced creates complaints. We confirm the date and window with the concierge or superintendent, book the service elevator, protect floors and finish before residents are back in the lobby in numbers.

challenges.title: Consistency across a portfolio
challenges.body: A manager running eight buildings does not want eight different looks and eight vendors. We hold a standard scheme for your portfolio, vary tree size by lobby, install on one schedule, send one invoice and keep the inventory for every building labelled in one warehouse.

spaces.title: Main lobby and reception
spaces.body: A decorated pre-lit tree, usually 7 to 12 ft depending on the ceiling, in a scheme that suits the lobby finishes, with garland on the concierge desk and a wreath on the glass. Placed where residents and visitors see it from the doors without blocking the mail room or the elevator call.

spaces.title: Entrance vestibule and canopy
spaces.body: Lit garland over the vestibule doors, wreaths outside, and the entrance canopy edge outlined in warm-white LED with wrapped columns. The canopy outline is the piece residents mention most because it is what they see coming home after dark. It runs on a photocell.

spaces.title: Elevator lobby and mail room
spaces.body: Smaller accent trees, lit gift boxes or a lit planter beside the elevators and a wreath at the mail room, so the decor continues as residents move through the ground floor. These pieces are secured, low-profile and out of the path to the elevator doors.

spaces.title: Courtyard and grounds
spaces.body: Tree wrapping in the courtyard, lit cone trees along the walk, hedges and planters lit at the entrance and roofline accents on a low-rise or townhouse block. Cone trees are staked and set back from plow and shovel routes, and everything is on a timer with the entrance.

spaces.title: Facade and roofline
spaces.body: For towers and mid-rises, roofline and podium outlines in warm white or a building colour, installed from a lift at night with the drive kept clear. On a townhouse or low-rise community, roofline lighting across the entrance block ties the whole property together.

programs.name: Essentials
programs.body: A lobby that looks finished for a modest budget: one decorated pre-lit tree sized to the ceiling, a wreath on the entrance glass and garland on the concierge desk. Installed in one visit and stored in January.
includes: Decorated pre-lit lobby tree, 7 to 9 ft

programs.name: Signature
programs.body: A taller lobby tree with accent trees, lit planters at the doors, garland over the vestibule, decor at the elevators and the entrance canopy outlined so the building reads from the street after dark.
includes: Lobby tree 9 to 12 ft with accent trees
Entrance canopy outline and column wraps

programs.name: Landmark
programs.body: A full-property program for larger communities: atrium or double-height lobby tree, courtyard tree wrapping and cone trees, podium or roofline outline and a consistent scheme across every building in the portfolio under one multi-year agreement.
includes: Lobby or atrium tree 12 to 16+ ft
Courtyard tree wrapping and cone trees

timeline.what: Site visit with the property manager, lobby measurements and photos, and a written proposal with reference images ready for the next board meeting.
Board approval and dates reserved. For portfolios, one schedule across all buildings. Inventory is pulled, tested and labelled per building in our warehouse.
Installation booked with the concierge or superintendent, service elevator reserved, floors protected, done overnight or in a quiet weekday window.
Display runs on timers. Residents' reports go through the concierge to us and any fault is fixed at no charge, usually within a business day.
Takedown in the first three weeks on a date the manager chooses, elevator rebooked, decor labelled and stored in our warehouse for next season.

faqs.question: What does a condo lobby Christmas decorator typically charge?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site visit or lobby photos with a ceiling height. As a typical range, a 9 ft decorated pre-lit lobby tree with installation, maintenance, removal and storage commonly starts around $1,500 per season. Accent trees, planters, vestibule garland and a canopy outline add to that, and multi-year agreements lock the price. Portfolio pricing applies when a manager books several buildings on one schedule. These are typical figures, not quotes.

faqs.question: How do you work around the concierge and the service elevator?
faqs.answer: We confirm the date and time window with the concierge or superintendent in advance, book the service elevator and loading dock through the building's normal process and arrive with floor protection. Most lobby installs run overnight or in a quiet mid-morning window and take a few hours. The concierge gets our contact number for the season so resident reports about the tree come straight to us.

faqs.question: Is the decor safe for a lobby full of residents, kids and dogs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Trees sit on weighted bases and are tied off where height requires, ornaments are shatterproof and wired on, cords run under covers or behind the skirt and nothing narrows the accessible route or blocks a door closer, exit sign or pull station. Lighting is low-draw LED on a timer set to lobby hours. If something is knocked or pulled loose, we come and fix it at no charge.

faqs.question: Can you give every building in our portfolio the same look?
faqs.answer: Yes, and property managers running several buildings usually prefer that. We set one scheme, vary tree height by lobby, install the portfolio on one schedule and send one invoice. Inventory for each building is labelled separately in our warehouse so the right tree goes back to the right lobby. Certificates of insurance and WSIB clearance are provided once for the whole portfolio each season.

faqs.question: Do we need to provide storage for the tree in January?
faqs.answer: No. Takedown, labelling and storage in our climate-controlled warehouse are included in every program. The building gives up no locker, mechanical room or parking stall, and the superintendent never handles a box. Trees and lighting are tested and refurbished over the summer so they work on install night, and your date is held before new clients are booked.

faqs.question: What insurance do you carry for work in a condo building?
faqs.answer: Our crews are insured and WSIB-compliant, and we provide a certificate of insurance naming the condominium corporation and the management company on request before the first install. We can also provide replacement values for leased decor so the corporation's broker can note it as property of others on site. All of this is standard paperwork for us, so the manager does not have to chase it.

ctaTitle: Get a proposal ready for your next board meeting
ctaBody: Send a photo of the lobby and the ceiling height and we will reply within one business day with a tree size, a scheme and a per-season price you can table with the board. Call 519-266-6796 to talk it through.

name: Plazas & Shopping Centres

title: Shopping Center Holiday Lighting Company | Ontario
metaDescription: Shopping center holiday lighting company for plazas and malls in Ontario. Giant trees, lot and boulevard lighting, Santa sets, overnight installs.
h1: Shopping center holiday lighting company for plazas and malls
intro: A shopping center holiday lighting company is judged from the road. We light plazas and enclosed malls across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara so the centre reads as the place to shop from the moment a driver sees the pylon sign: giant trees in the courtyard, parking-lot and boulevard trees wrapped, storefront rooflines outlined and, inside, a Santa set and village that bring families back through December.

Commercial plaza Christmas tree installation is the usual starting point. A giant lit tree at the main entrance, engineered for wind and set clear of plow routes, with lighting that carries from the sign to the storefronts so there is no dark gap in the middle. Enclosed malls add a Santa photo set, a village display and concourse trees sized to the court.

All of it is built overnight after close with lifts, traffic control and a crew that is off the lot before the first delivery. Maintenance is included at no charge, which matters when thousands of shoppers walk past a display each day. January takedown, labelled storage and multi-year pricing that locks dates before Black Friday are standard. Tenants get a consistent look across every bay.

challenges.title: Foot traffic through December
challenges.body: The display has to work from early November to the week after Christmas with no dark nights, because tenants notice and shoppers compare. We use commercial-grade product, put every circuit on a timer or photocell, check exposed lighting after storms and fix any fault at no charge, usually the same day.

challenges.title: Lifts, traffic and overnight access
challenges.body: Rooflines, lot trees and giant trees all need a lift, and the lot cannot be closed. We install after close with cones, a spotter and a plan for fire lanes and loading, and the lift is gone before deliveries start. Interior builds in a mall court run after the doors lock and are opened each morning.

challenges.title: Tenant expectations and the pylon sign
challenges.body: A lit sign with a dark drive and lit storefronts with a dark courtyard both look unfinished. We design continuity from the pylon sign along the boulevard to the entrance tree and across the storefront rooflines, so the whole frontage reads as one centre. Tenants see a consistent look rather than a patchwork.

challenges.title: Power across a large site
challenges.body: Lot trees and boulevard medians are often far from an outlet. We survey lamp-post receptacles and exterior circuits in summer, split loads so breakers are not near their limit, run weatherproof feeds where needed and tell you in the quote if your electrician should add a receptacle before install.

spaces.title: Entrance and courtyard giant tree
spaces.body: A giant pre-lit or cone tree at the main entrance or courtyard, with a star topper and a lit base, often in the centre's colours. Trees are engineered for wind, ballasted or staked, set back from plow routes and built from a lift overnight on their own timed circuit.

spaces.title: Parking lot and boulevard trees
spaces.body: Rows of lot evergreens and median or boulevard trees wrapped in warm white or colour so the drive in is lit, not just the storefronts. Installed from a bucket truck at night with cones and a spotter, powered from lamp-post receptacles or dedicated weatherproof feeds.

spaces.title: Storefront rooflines and columns
spaces.body: C9 or mini LED along the storefront roofline, columns wrapped in garland, wreaths over entrances and posts. We run one continuous look across the whole frontage so no tenant's bay is dark and the roofline reads from the far side of the lot.

spaces.title: Santa set and photo moment
spaces.body: For enclosed malls, a modular Santa cabin or village set with seating, backdrop, queue fencing and a photo podium, framed by decorated trees. The camera angle is designed first and the set is placed so the queue never blocks a storefront or an exit.

spaces.title: Atrium and concourse
spaces.body: A giant atrium tree under the skylight, concourse trees sized to the court, sleigh and reindeer features and garland on railings and planters, all built overnight and secured against carts and crowds. Decor stays clear of sprinklers, exits and storefront lines.

programs.name: Essentials
programs.body: For a strip plaza or small centre: the entrance tree, the storefront roofline outlined end to end and wreaths at the main entrances, installed overnight and serviced all season so the frontage reads from the road.
includes: Timers and photocells on every circuit

programs.name: Signature
programs.body: A full exterior program: giant entrance tree in the centre's colours, boulevard and lot trees wrapped, rooflines and columns lit across every bay, and lighting from the pylon sign through to the doors so there is no dark gap.
includes: Rooflines and columns across all bays

programs.name: Landmark
programs.body: For enclosed malls and large centres: everything in Signature plus a Santa photo set, village display, atrium tree and concourse decor inside, and the option of an animated pixel light show on the facade or courtyard tree.
includes: Santa photo set with queue fencing and podium

timeline.what: Site visit with the property or marketing manager, footage and tree counts, lamp-post and outlet survey, lift access and a written design with photos.
Scope approved, dates reserved and any new receptacles handled by your electrician. Inventory is pulled, tested and labelled per site in our warehouse.
Overnight installation: lot and boulevard trees, rooflines and the giant tree from lifts with traffic control, then interior sets after close, lit before Black Friday.
Display runs on timers and photocells. Storm checks on exposed lighting, Santa set adjustments on request and any fault fixed at no charge.
Takedown in the first three weeks, interior sets first so the court is clear for January sales, then exterior from lifts, with everything labelled and stored.

faqs.question: What does commercial plaza Christmas tree installation involve?
faqs.answer: We size the tree to the courtyard or entrance, choose a lit cone tree or a giant pre-lit tree, confirm the base is clear of plow routes and fire lanes, and check wind exposure. The tree is built overnight from a lift, ballasted or staked, topped with a star and wired to its own timed circuit. Maintenance is included all season, and in January it comes down and goes into labelled storage in our warehouse.

faqs.question: How do you install without closing the parking lot?
faqs.answer: Exterior work runs after close, when the lot is empty. We cone off the area under the lift, keep a spotter on traffic, leave fire lanes and loading docks clear and move bay by bay along the roofline. By the time the first delivery truck arrives, the lift is gone and the lights are set to come on that evening. Interior mall builds run after the doors lock and the court is opened each morning.

faqs.question: What does a shopping centre holiday lighting program typically cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site visit. As a typical range, exterior programs start from a few thousand dollars for a small plaza roofline and entrance tree and run to tens of thousands for a large centre with lot trees, boulevard wrapping and a giant tree. Enclosed-mall interiors with a Santa set and village are five-figure programs per season. Footage, tree count, lift work and term length are the drivers. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: Can you build a Santa photo set in our mall?
faqs.answer: Yes. We design and build modular Santa cabin and village sets from our own inventory, with seating, a backdrop, queue fencing, a photo podium and decorated trees around it. The set is designed around the camera angle and placed with your operations team so the queue never blocks a storefront or an exit. It goes up overnight across two or three nights and is removed first in January so the court is clear for sales.

faqs.question: What happens when a section of roofline goes dark in December?
faqs.answer: Call or text us and a crew comes with the lift, usually the same day in December, traces the fault to the failed string, plug or fuse and replaces it from stock. There is no charge; maintenance is part of every program. After major wind or ice we check exposed rooflines, lot trees and the giant tree without being asked. Because the product is ours, repairs are a swap, not a wait for parts.

faqs.question: Do you provide insurance certificates and traffic plans for the landlord?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our crews are insured and WSIB-compliant, and we provide a certificate of insurance naming the landlord and the management company before the first install. For lift work near traffic we supply a simple plan showing cones, the lift position, spotters and which lanes stay open. Replacement values for leased displays are available for the landlord's broker so the Santa set or giant tree can be noted as property of others on site.

ctaTitle: Light the centre before Black Friday
ctaBody: Plaza and mall installs need lifts and overnight slots, and those fill from October. Call 519-266-6796 or send a site plan and photos and we will reply within one business day with a design and a per-season price.

h1: Holiday decorating for office buildings and corporate campuses
intro: Commercial holiday decorating services for office buildings start with the lobby, because that is where every tenant, client and courier forms an opinion about the building. We decorate office towers and corporate campuses across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara: lobby and atrium trees, elevator-lobby and reception decor, lit entrances and tree wrapping along the approach, installed overnight so the workday is never interrupted.

A typical downtown program is a 12 to 20 ft tree against the marble or granite feature wall, accent trees at the vestibule, lit gift boxes beside the elevators, garland over the doors and the entrance trees on the sidewalk wrapped in warm white. Colour schemes follow the lobby finishes or the landlord's standard across a portfolio. Reference photos come from our own office installs.

Tenant appreciation is the usual reason an office landlord adds decor, and consistency is the usual reason a corporate campus does. Either way, everything is our own inventory, maintenance is included at no charge, takedown runs in the first three weeks of January and the decor is stored in our warehouse, labelled by building, until next season. Security gets crew names and certificates of insurance ahead of install night.

challenges.title: No disruption to the workday
challenges.body: Office lobbies are busiest from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., and a lift in the lobby at noon is unacceptable. We install overnight or on a weekend, coordinate with security and the building operator, book the loading dock and freight elevator and leave the lobby clean before the first tenant badges in.

challenges.title: Security and after-hours access
challenges.body: Downtown towers need crew names in advance, escorts and a sign-in process. We provide the crew list, vehicle details and certificate of insurance ahead of the install night, follow the building's contractor rules and keep the property manager informed of arrival and departure times.

challenges.title: Consistency across buildings
challenges.body: Landlords with several buildings want one look that scales with the lobby, not a different vendor and a different tree in each. We set a standard scheme, vary tree height and accent pieces by building, install on one schedule and keep one labelled inventory for the portfolio in our warehouse.

challenges.title: Tenant appreciation that looks intentional
challenges.body: A lone tree in a 30 ft lobby looks like an afterthought. We design to the scale of the space: the right height for the ceiling, accent trees to fill the width, garland that follows the architecture and exterior lighting that carries the look to the sidewalk so tenants see it on the way in.

spaces.title: Main lobby and atrium
spaces.body: A 12 to 20+ ft decorated tree sized to the ceiling and set against the feature wall or centred under the atrium, flanked by lit accent trees. Built from a lift overnight, secured against tipping, with lighting on a timer set to building hours and a scheme matched to the stone and metal of the lobby.

spaces.title: Elevator lobbies

spaces.title: Entrance vestibule
spaces.body: Lit garland arched over the glass doors, wreaths on the vestibule and planters at the entrance dressed with evergreen, birch and lit branches. Attachments suit glass and metal, and nothing interferes with door closers, exit hardware or the accessible entrance.

spaces.title: Sidewalk trees and planters
spaces.body: Street trees and sidewalk planters outside the tower wrapped in warm white with blue or coloured accent lighting in the beds, powered from the building's exterior circuits on a photocell. Installed from a lift at night with the sidewalk kept open for pedestrians.

spaces.title: Campus entrances and grounds
spaces.body: For suburban campuses, roofline outlines on the main building, tree wrapping along the entrance drive, lit cone trees at the sign and lighting in the courtyard between wings. Lifts work after hours with the drive kept clear for shift changes and deliveries.

faqs.question: How do you install in an office lobby without disrupting tenants?
faqs.answer: We work overnight or on a weekend, coordinated with security and the building operator. The crew signs in, books the freight elevator and loading dock, protects the lobby floor, builds and decorates the tree from a lift and is gone before the first tenant arrives. Most single-lobby programs are complete in one night. Sidewalk tree wrapping runs at the same time from a lift outside with the sidewalk kept open.

faqs.question: Can you handle the same look across all our buildings?
faqs.answer: Yes. Landlords with several buildings get one scheme, scaled to each lobby, installed on one schedule with one invoice. Each building's inventory is labelled separately in our warehouse so the right tree returns to the right lobby. Certificates of insurance and WSIB clearance are issued once per season for the portfolio, and the property manager has one contact for every site.

faqs.question: What does an office lobby holiday program typically cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site visit. Tree height, lift work, garland footage and term length are the drivers. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: What are your requirements for security and after-hours access?
faqs.answer: We provide crew names, vehicle details and a certificate of insurance in advance, follow the building's contractor sign-in and escort rules and confirm arrival and departure times with security. We bring our own lifts, floor protection, cords and timers so nothing is borrowed from the building. If your tower needs a specific form or a pre-install meeting with the operator, we do that during the planning stage in September.

faqs.question: What happens if the tree lights fail in the middle of December?
faqs.answer: Security or the property manager calls or texts us and we fix it at no charge, scheduled after hours and usually within a business day. Our trees are wired in sections, so a fault takes out one band of lights rather than the tree, and the crew carries replacement sections. Ribbon pulled loose or a planter knocked by a courier are handled the same way. Maintenance is part of every program.

faqs.question: Do you decorate corporate campuses outside the downtown core?
faqs.answer: Yes. Suburban campuses in Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara get the same program: lobby trees in each building, roofline outlines on the main facade, tree wrapping along the entrance drive and lit cone trees at the sign. Exterior work runs from bucket trucks after hours with the drive kept clear for shift changes. For sites outside our daily range, plans and photos are enough to start a design.

h1: Property management holiday lighting contractor for portfolios
intro: A property management holiday lighting contractor should make a portfolio easier to run, not add a vendor per site. We handle holiday lighting and decor across many properties for property managers and REITs in Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara: one contact, one schedule, one invoice, standard specs that scale from a strip plaza to an office tower, and insurance certificates issued once for the whole portfolio.

Standardization is what makes a portfolio program work. We set a spec per property type, such as roofline and entrance tree for retail, lobby tree and vestibule garland for office and residential, and price it per site so a new acquisition can be added mid-season at a known rate. Site-level details, lift access, power, security, are recorded once and reused every year.

Everything is our own inventory, so maintenance is included at no charge across every site and a dark roofline at one property does not become a purchase order. Takedown runs in the first three weeks of January, inventory is labelled per building in our warehouse and multi-year agreements lock pricing and dates for the term. Site staff get one number to call all season.

challenges.title: Too many vendors, too many invoices
challenges.body: A portfolio with a different lighting company at every site means a different quote format, a different insurance certificate and a different phone call when something fails. We consolidate the whole portfolio under one agreement, one schedule, one contact for site staff and one invoice per season or per site, as your accounting prefers.

challenges.title: Budget approvals a year ahead
challenges.body: Holiday decor is approved in the spring budget for the following season, so prices have to hold. Multi-year agreements lock the per-site price and the install dates for the term, and we provide a per-property breakdown that drops into an operating budget or a common-area recovery schedule.

challenges.title: Insurance, WSIB and compliance paperwork
challenges.body: Every owner wants a certificate of insurance naming the right entities, a WSIB clearance certificate and proof the crew is trained for lift work. We issue these once per season for the whole portfolio, update them when a property changes hands and keep them on file so site staff are not chasing documents in November.

challenges.title: Knowing what happened at each site
challenges.body: Managers need to answer an owner's question about a property they have not visited. We send install photos per site, log every service visit with what was found and fixed, and provide a season summary so you can show what was delivered at each address without driving there.

spaces.title: Retail plazas and storefronts
spaces.body: Roofline outlines across every bay, column wraps, entrance wreaths and a lit tree at the main entrance, with lot and boulevard trees wrapped on larger centres. One spec across the retail portfolio so tenants at every plaza get the same standard and the look reads from the road.

spaces.title: Office buildings

spaces.body: Condo and apartment lobbies with trees, entrance canopies outlined, courtyard tree wrapping and cone trees, scheduled around concierges and superintendents. faqs.question: What does a property management holiday lighting contractor provide that a local installer does not?
faqs.answer: One agreement, one schedule, one invoice and one contact for every site, instead of a vendor per property. Standard specs per property type so pricing is predictable and new acquisitions can be added at a known rate. Certificates of insurance and WSIB clearance issued once for the portfolio. Install photos and a service log per site for owner reporting. And our own inventory at every property, so maintenance is included everywhere at no charge.

faqs.question: How do you price a portfolio?
faqs.answer: Per site, from a standard spec for each property type, so a plaza, an office lobby and a residential tower each have a known per-season price. The portfolio total is quoted for one season and for a multi-year term that locks the rates and dates. We provide a per-property breakdown for budgets and common-area recovery. Typical ranges run from a few thousand per retail site to five figures for a flagship lobby or large centre, as typical figures rather than quotes.

faqs.question: Can you issue insurance certificates for every property owner?
faqs.answer: Yes. We issue a certificate of insurance naming each owner entity and the management company before the first install, along with a WSIB clearance certificate, and we update them when a property is acquired or sold during the term. Replacement values for leased decor are available so each owner's broker can note it as property of others on site. This is standard paperwork for us and is handled in September, not November.

faqs.question: What happens when a site reports a fault?
faqs.answer: Site staff, a concierge or a tenant coordinator calls or texts one number. We schedule a visit after hours, usually within a business day and often the same day in December, fix the fault from stock on the truck at no charge and log what was found and done. The manager gets the log entry, not a service invoice. Exposed exterior sites are also checked after major storms without a call.

faqs.question: Can you add a newly acquired building mid-season?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the specs are standard, a new acquisition is added at the agreed per-site rate for its property type. We survey it from photos or a quick visit, pull matching inventory from our warehouse and slot it into the schedule. Early in the season that usually means lit within two weeks; in December it depends on crew availability, and we tell you honestly what is possible.

faqs.question: What reporting do you provide at the end of the season?
faqs.answer: Install photos per property, a service log with every visit, what was found and what was fixed, and a season summary across the portfolio that you can forward to owners or an asset manager. For multi-year agreements the summary also notes any spec changes recommended for next season, such as a receptacle an electrician should add or a tree that should move because of a new plow route.

title: Commercial Christmas Light Installation for Storefronts
metaDescription: Christmas light installation for restaurants, retail and dealerships in Ontario. Storefront rooflines, patio bistro lights, wreaths and lot lighting.
h1: Holiday lighting and decor for restaurants, retail and dealerships
intro: Commercial Christmas light installation for a restaurant, store or dealership has a deadline the landlord's program does not: your busiest weeks start the day after Black Friday, and the storefront has to be lit before then. We light storefronts, patios, entrances and lots across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara, installed overnight so you never close a door or lose a parking space.

The usual program is the roofline or gable outlined in warm-white C9 or mini LED, columns wrapped in lit garland, a wreath over the door and bistro string lights across the patio. Interior trees and window moments bring the look inside for diners and shoppers. Dealerships add lot lighting so the showroom and the front row of vehicles read from the road after dark.

Everything is our own commercial-grade inventory, so maintenance is included at no charge; a dark section on opening week is fixed the same day. Takedown runs in the first three weeks of January, the decor is stored in our warehouse and returning businesses get their install slot held before Black Friday. Landlord approvals and certificates of insurance are handled by us, not by your manager, so the only thing you do is pick a date.

challenges.title: The opening-week deadline
challenges.body: Seasonal revenue starts in late November and a storefront that is lit in mid-December has missed half of it. We schedule restaurant, retail and dealership installs from October onward and hold your slot once you book. Returning businesses are scheduled first, which is why early confirmation matters.

challenges.title: Installing without closing
challenges.body: A lift in front of the door at lunch costs you customers. We install after close or before open, work from the lot or the sidewalk with cones and a spotter, keep the entrance, drive-through and patio open and are gone before the first customer arrives. Interior trees go up after close in one visit.

challenges.title: Landlord and plaza rules
challenges.body: Tenants in a plaza often need landlord approval for anything attached to the building. We use clips and mounts that leave no marks, provide a certificate of insurance to the landlord on request and can coordinate with the plaza's own lighting program so your storefront fits the centre rather than fighting it.

challenges.title: Power on a small site
challenges.body: A storefront may have one exterior outlet, and a patio may have none. We survey what exists, run weatherproof feeds from the nearest protected circuit, put everything on a photocell or timer and tell you in the quote if your electrician should add a receptacle before install.

spaces.title: Storefront roofline and gable
spaces.body: C9 or mini LED along the roofline, gable or parapet, wreaths on the gable or over the door and columns wrapped in lit garland. We measure the footage, pick the clip for your fascia and run the feed to a protected outlet on a photocell so the storefront is lit from dusk every day.

spaces.title: Patio and terrace
spaces.body: Bistro string lights across the patio, lit cone trees at the corners, garland on railings and planters dressed for winter, so the terrace is lit through the season. Lighting is on the same timer as the storefront and rated for outdoor use through ice and snow.

spaces.title: Entrance and windows
spaces.body: A lit wreath and garland framing the door, wreaths in the windows and a window moment such as a small decorated tree or lit planter that reads from the sidewalk and in the photos customers take. Attachments suit glass, metal and timber without marks.

spaces.title: Dining room and sales floor
spaces.body: A decorated pre-lit tree at the host stand or in the showroom, garland on railings and counters and ornaments in your brand colours, placed clear of service paths, heat sources and the sales floor traffic. Installed after close and serviced all season.

spaces.title: Dealership lot and signage
spaces.body: Lot trees and the frontage evergreens wrapped, cone trees along the entrance, the showroom roofline outlined and lighting at the pylon sign so the dealership reads from the road after dark. Installed from a bucket truck at night with the lot kept open and vehicles untouched.

programs.name: Essentials
programs.body: A lit storefront for a single location: the roofline or gable outlined, a wreath over the door and the columns or posts wrapped, installed before Black Friday in one after-hours visit and stored in January.
includes: Photocell or timer on every circuit

programs.name: Signature
programs.body: Storefront plus patio and interior: the roofline outlined, bistro lights across the patio, cone trees at the entrance, wreaths in the windows and a decorated tree at the host stand or on the sales floor.
includes: Patio bistro lights and cone trees

programs.name: Landmark
programs.body: For flagship restaurants, breweries, multi-location retailers and dealerships: full exterior and interior program, lot and frontage tree wrapping, signage lighting, brand colour scheme and a multi-location schedule with one invoice.

timeline.what: A site visit or storefront photos, footage and power survey, landlord requirements noted and a written design with reference photos.
Scope approved, install slot reserved ahead of Black Friday and a certificate of insurance sent to the landlord if the lease requires one.
Overnight or early-morning install with the entrance, drive-through and patio kept open, lit and on a photocell before you open.
Storefront runs on timers through the busiest weeks. Any fault fixed at no charge, same day where possible, with storm checks on exposed rooflines.
Takedown in the first three weeks after close, decor labelled and stored in our warehouse, and your slot held for next season.

faqs.question: Can you light our storefront before Black Friday?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you book early. Installs run from October and restaurant, retail and dealership slots are scheduled ahead of Black Friday as a matter of course. Returning businesses have their dates held first, so the earlier a new location confirms, the better its slot. If you call in mid-November we will tell you honestly what is still possible rather than promising a date we cannot keep.

faqs.question: What does commercial Christmas light installation for a storefront typically cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site visit or storefront photos. As a typical range, exterior programs start from a few thousand dollars for a storefront roofline, entrance wreath and column wraps, and rise with patio lighting, interior trees, lot tree wrapping and signage. Multi-location retailers and dealerships are priced per site on one agreement. Footage, tree count and lift work are the drivers. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: Do you install while we are open?
faqs.answer: No. We install after close or before open so the entrance, drive-through, patio and parking stay available to customers. Exterior work runs from the lot or sidewalk with cones and a spotter, and interior trees go up after close in a single visit. On a dealership lot we work at night with vehicles untouched and the showroom roofline done from a bucket truck.

faqs.question: Will the lights damage our fascia, patio or windows?
faqs.answer: No. We use purpose-made clips for shingle, metal fascia, stone and timber, wrapped ties for columns and posts, and suction or edge mounts for glass. We do not drill into finishes without written approval, and everything comes down with the decor in January. For tenants, that also keeps the landlord happy. Patio bistro lights are hung on tensioned cable rated for ice and wind rather than stapled to the structure.

faqs.question: What happens if a section goes dark on a Friday night in December?
faqs.answer: Call or text us and we come out, usually the same day in December, trace the fault to the failed string, plug or fuse and replace it from stock. There is no charge; maintenance is part of every program. Photocells and timers are reset if a power blip knocked them out. After major wind or ice we check exposed rooflines without a call, because an unlit storefront in the busiest week is the last thing you need.

faqs.question: Do you light dealership lots?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dealership programs usually wrap the frontage evergreens and lot trees, line the entrance with cone trees, outline the showroom roofline and light the pylon sign so the front row of vehicles and the showroom read from the road after dark. Work runs at night from a bucket truck with the lot open and vehicles untouched. Brand colours are matched on samples, and multi-store groups are scheduled on one agreement.

h1: Holiday lighting for municipalities, BIAs and downtown districts
intro: Commercial holiday decorating services for a municipality or BIA have to survive procurement, a council or board vote and a tree-lighting event with the whole town watching. We light downtown streets, town squares, parks and civic buildings across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara: street-tree wrapping along the main street, a town-square tree, park pathway displays, community-hall outlines and animated light shows.

Downtown work means traffic plans, lamp-post power, bucket trucks on a main street at night and crews who understand that the sidewalk stays open. We provide tender-ready specifications with linear footage, tree counts, product details and a maintenance scope, certificates of insurance and WSIB clearance, and a traffic management plan for the install nights. Public works staff are kept informed block by block.

Everything is our own commercial-grade inventory, so maintenance through the season is included at no charge, including after ice storms and plow damage. Takedown runs in the first three weeks of January or later if the town wants a winter festival lit, and inventory is labelled and stored in our warehouse. Multi-year agreements lock pricing for the budget cycle. The town-square tree is always scheduled first.

challenges.title: Procurement and tender-ready specs
challenges.body: Councils and boards need a specification they can put to tender or approve under a purchasing bylaw. We provide footage, tree counts, product type, controls, maintenance scope, takedown and storage terms and insurance requirements in a format that can be dropped into an RFQ, and we quote the same scope honestly.

challenges.title: Traffic, sidewalks and lamp-post power
challenges.body: Main-street tree wrapping means a bucket truck in a live lane at night. We supply a traffic plan with cones, signage and spotters, keep the sidewalk open, work after the restaurants close and power the trees from lamp-post receptacles or circuits your public works staff identify with us in the summer survey.

challenges.title: The tree-lighting event
challenges.body: The town-square tree has to be lit, tested and on a switch or controller by the event date, with everything else in the square complete around it. We schedule the square first, test the circuit with your staff the day before and can run the switch-on from a controller so the moment works.

challenges.title: Ice, plows and a long season
challenges.body: Municipal displays are up from November to January or later, in the open, next to plow routes and salt. We stake and set back cone trees, tie off wraps so they do not slip, elevate connections and check exposed streets after major storms without a call, fixing anything at no charge.

spaces.title: Downtown street trees
spaces.body: Boulevard and sidewalk trees along the main street wrapped in warm white or a BIA colour, trunk and canopy, with red ornament balls or accents where the district wants them. Installed from a bucket truck at night under a traffic plan and powered from lamp-post receptacles on photocells.

spaces.title: Town square and civic tree
spaces.body: A large outdoor tree, either a lit natural evergreen or a giant cone tree, beside the memorial, clock or town hall, with a star topper and a lit base. Engineered for wind, staked or ballasted, on its own circuit and ready for the switch-on at the tree-lighting event.

spaces.title: Parks and pathways
spaces.body: Mature trees along park walkways wrapped so the path is lit end to end, gazebos and pavilions outlined, light figures and entrance arches placed for photos. Timers run dusk to late evening so the park is usable after dark without the lights burning all night.

spaces.title: Community halls and civic buildings
spaces.body: Roofline outlines on the town hall, arena, library or community centre, lit cone trees at the entrance, wreaths over the doors and, where the building suits it, a pixel light show on the facade. Installed from lifts after hours with the entrance kept open.

spaces.title: Light shows and feature displays
spaces.body: Animated pixel light shows on a pavilion or facade synced to music, giant cone trees in a plaza, walk-through tunnels and lit sculptures for a winter festival. Shows run on a schedule the town sets with a static look between shows so the space is never dark.

programs.name: Essentials
programs.body: A lit main street for a BIA or small town: street trees wrapped along the core blocks, wreaths or accents on lamp posts and the town-square tree lit for the event, installed under a traffic plan and serviced all season.
includes: Traffic plan and certificates of insurance

programs.name: Signature
programs.body: A downtown and park program: more blocks of street trees, the civic building roofline outlined, cone trees at entrances, a park pathway display with a lit gazebo or pavilion and a tested switch-on for the tree-lighting event.
includes: Switch-on support for the tree-lighting event

programs.name: Landmark
programs.body: A destination program for a winter festival or regional town: everything in Signature plus an animated pixel light show, walk-through tunnel or giant cone tree, feature displays across the park and a multi-year agreement that holds pricing through the budget cycle.
includes: Walk-through tunnel or giant cone tree
Park feature displays and light figures

timeline.what: Site walk with public works or the BIA coordinator, tree counts, lamp-post power survey, tree-lighting date confirmed, and a tender-ready spec and design submitted for approval.
Approval or award, dates reserved, traffic plan, certificate of insurance and WSIB clearance submitted, inventory pulled and labelled for the municipality.
Night installs under the traffic plan: the square first, then street trees, civic buildings and parks, with the switch-on circuit tested with your staff before the event.
Display runs on photocells and timers. Storm and plow-damage checks after major weather, light-show schedule adjusted on request, any fault fixed at no charge.
Takedown in the first three weeks of January, or after a winter festival if the town wants it, with inventory labelled and stored for next season.

faqs.question: Can you provide a specification we can put to tender?
faqs.answer: Yes. We provide a written specification with tree counts and locations, linear footage, product type and colour, controls, the maintenance scope and response time, takedown and storage terms, traffic management and insurance requirements. It can be used in an RFQ or attached to a purchasing-bylaw approval. We quote the same scope and tell you honestly if a line in a tender would be better written another way.

faqs.question: How do you handle traffic and sidewalks on a main street install?
faqs.answer: We provide a traffic management plan for the install nights showing lane closures, cones, signage and spotters, and we work after the restaurants and bars close so the street is quiet. The sidewalk stays open with the bucket truck positioned to keep pedestrians clear of the work. Public works staff are kept informed of which blocks are being done each night, and the plan is adjusted around events or parades.

faqs.question: Where does the power come from for street trees?
faqs.answer: Most downtown street trees are powered from receptacles on the lamp posts or from circuits in the boulevard that public works already uses for banners and summer lighting. We survey those with your staff in the summer, split loads so no circuit is near its limit, elevate and weatherproof the connections and put everything on photocells. If blocks have no power, we say so in the spec so the town can plan receptacles.

faqs.question: Can you light the town-square tree for our tree-lighting event?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we schedule the square first for that reason. The tree is lit, the circuit is tested with your staff the day before and the switch-on can be run from a controller or a simple switch at the stage so the moment works on cue. If the event includes a light show on a pavilion or facade, we program a launch sequence and run it on a schedule afterwards.

faqs.question: What insurance and safety documents do you provide a municipality?
faqs.answer: A certificate of insurance naming the municipality or BIA, a WSIB clearance certificate, a traffic management plan for the install and takedown nights and confirmation that crews are trained for aerial lift work. We are insured commercial holiday decorators and this is standard paperwork for us, provided in September with the specification so it is on file before procurement closes. Replacement values for leased displays are available for the town's insurer.

faqs.question: What does a downtown or municipal holiday lighting program typically cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted from a site walk and the tender spec. As a typical range, a few blocks of street-tree wrapping and a town-square tree start from several thousand dollars per season, and programs with park displays, civic building outlines and animated light shows run to tens of thousands. Tree count, block length, lift work and term length are the drivers, and multi-year agreements lock pricing for the budget cycle. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

ctaBody: Summer is when municipal specs get written and dates get reserved. Call 519-266-6796 or send us the blocks, the square and the park you want lit and we will reply within one business day with a specification and a typical range.
